title: Chapter 65
content:
Opening the crates Park Tae-soo delivered that afternoon, Jakyeong stood in stunned silence. Beside him, Wang Han and Wang Ryun let out low whistles of genuine awe.

Packed inside high-density foam were rows of high-grade tactical arms and precision gear—the exact calibers and platforms Jakyeong had seen in the basement armory a year ago.

While they inspected the loadout, Tae-soo placed a sleek key fob onto the glass coffee table.

"This is the vehicle assigned for your operational use. Please use this for all transit."

Ryun scooped up the fob, his eyes widening at the crest. It was a high-performance, armored foreign sedan.

"And if there are any additional logistics or specialized munitions required," Tae-soo added smoothly, "let me know and I will have them requisitioned immediately."

Before turning to leave, Tae-soo handed a boutique shopping bag across to Jakyeong.

"President Kang asked me to deliver this directly to you."

Once Tae-soo bowed out, Jakyeong opened the parcel. Inside was a factory-sealed, flagship-tier smartphone. Given that Il-hyun had drowned his previous phone in the pool, replacing it made practical sense—though Jakyeong made a mental note to tear the casing apart down to the motherboard to check for hardware bugs and tracking beacons before powering it on.

Looking at the luxury gear, Ryun was visibly wavering. With a payout this massive, plus luxury cars and free hardware... maybe running off halfway through isn't the move. What if we just sign on for the full year?

He sneaked a glance at Jakyeong's stone-cold expression, immediately killing the thought. After the fistfight his loose mouth had sparked the night before, the atmosphere between the two was still walking a razor's edge.

"President Kang certainly doesn't mess around," Ryun muttered admiringly. "The man knows how to throw money at a problem."

Jakyeong didn't offer a syllable in response, quietly stripping down a sidearm to clean the firing pin with a cigarette clamped between his teeth. Ryun shot a helpless look toward Wang Han, who simply shook his head, silently advising him to leave the kid alone.

Stripped down to his briefs, Jakyeong lay flat on his back, staring blankly up at the ceiling molding.

Every piece of furniture shattered during their brawl had been replaced with brand-new, bespoke furnishings, and the bed frame had been upgraded to an even wider, plush king-sized mattress. Outside, torrential rain had pounded the estate since yesterday, keeping the air hot and thick, but the central climate control maintained a crisp, quiet chill throughout the suite.

Surprisingly, Kang Il-hyun hadn't shown his face once yesterday. When they crossed paths briefly at dawn, the man had offered nothing more than a polite, brief greeting. He hadn't reached out to touch him, nor had he dropped a single depraved innuendo or mocking quip.

It was a relief—yet the sudden, total silence felt deeply unsettling.

They say when a person changes overnight, their death is around the corner.

Dying would be convenient, but Jakyeong feared the man was merely bottling his lunacy, coiling back only to unleash an even more catastrophic wave of psychotic behavior.

Knock, knock.

Jakyeong lifted his head. The heavy latch clicked, and Kang Il-hyun appeared in the doorway.

Jakyeong’s brow knit instantly. He grabbed his discarded shirt from the nightstand, slipping his arms through the sleeves, when Il-hyun paused on the threshold, asking in a quiet, polite tone:

"May I come in?"

Jakyeong froze with his buttons half-done. He blinked, wondering if his ears were playing tricks on him. The man stood there, patiently waiting for verbal permission.

Meeting his unblinking stare, Il-hyun gently pulled the door shut behind him and stepped inside.

Faint yellowing bruises still colored his sharp jawline. In his right hand, he carried a steaming ceramic mug. Approaching the bed, he set the cup down onto the bedside table. A delicate, familiar herbal fragrance drifted into the air—Jakyeong’s preferred blend.

"I asked your brother," Il-hyun said softly. "He mentioned you liked this tea."

Jakyeong said nothing, keeping his guard up.

Il-hyun pulled an armchair over, settling down to meet Jakyeong's gaze with a sheepish, apologetic smile.

"I went too far the other night. No matter how angry I was... threatening to take a hatchet to your cock was completely out of line."

Jakyeong stared back in pure, unadulterated disbelief. You think that needs to be said, you lunatic? He wanted to curse the man into the ground, but engaging felt like a waste of breath.

Wishing the bastard would just vanish, Jakyeong noticed Il-hyun reach into his tailored jacket. Assuming another concealed weapon was about to surface, Jakyeong instinctively balled his fists—only for Il-hyun to withdraw something entirely unexpected.

He placed a small object beside the teacup.

It was a miniature elephant figurine, hand-carved from dark, fragrant timber with exquisite, delicate detail.

Watching Jakyeong stare at it, Il-hyun spoke with a soft, quiet cadence. "Saw it and thought of you. You like little trinkets like this, don't you?"

Jakyeong kept his jaw locked.

Il-hyun rose to his feet, hesitating for a rare, awkward beat. He reached out, his long fingers gently smoothing the dark hair from Jakyeong’s brow. Stunned by the tender contact, Jakyeong didn't pull away. Il-hyun stroked the strands once, lingering for half a second before drawing his hand back cleanly.

"Get some rest, then. Dream well."

Offering a warm, effortless smile, Il-hyun turned and walked out of the suite, latching the door quietly behind him.

Jakyeong blinked slowly, pinching his own cheek to confirm he wasn't dreaming.

Glancing between the steaming mug and the carved elephant, reality snapped into focus. Is he out of his goddamn mind? What is this game? The sudden gentleman routine didn't feel reassuring—it felt terrifying.

Suspicious that the man was eavesdropping in the hallway, Jakyeong yanked the door open. The corridor was empty. He checked the living room downstairs—completely deserted. Paranoid that fresh surveillance had been planted during the furniture replacement, he tore through the lamps, vents, and baseboards, but found nothing.

The suite was quiet, scented only by the calming herbal tea and the faint, lingering trace of Il-hyun's cologne.

Sitting on the edge of the mattress, Jakyeong picked up the little wooden elephant, glaring at it in the dim light.

What kind of trap are you setting this time?
Downstairs, the three operatives were sitting down to an early dinner when Il-hyun emerged from his quarters.

He had changed out of his business suit into a tailored black silk shirt, the monochrome styling lending his sharp, sculpted features an intensely brooding, decadent edge.

Jakyeong offered a fleeting glance before pointedly returning to his meal. Wang Han and Wang Ryun greeted him with respectful nods, but Jakyeong kept his head down, refusing to acknowledge the presence.

Il-hyun quietly informed the senior housekeeper that he wouldn't be dining at home tonight, offered a brief, polite farewell to the table, and walked out the front doors into the dark.

Jakyeong tracked the retreating silhouette through the corner of his eye.

Ryun nudged his elbow under the table. "Still haven't patched things up?"

Jakyeong didn't answer.

"Where's he off to, anyway? The vibe felt completely different."

The housekeeper stepped over, refilling their side dishes with a quiet, sorrowful smile.

"Today is the anniversary of his late mother's passing."

Jakyeong’s hand paused over his water glass. Unconsciously, his gaze drifted back toward the empty foyer.

He recalled the fragments Il-hyun had shared months ago—how his mother had lost her sanity and hung herself; how she had tried to drown Il-hyun in the pool as a child; and how the tragedy had started with Chairman Kang abducting a teenage girl to breed a tool for the syndicate.

Was that where his bottomless hatred began?

Jakyeong’s chopsticks moved slowly. Memories of his own dead mother surfaced, leaving his chest tight with tangled, suffocating thoughts.

The mark they were scheduled to eliminate in two days, Choi Man-sik, was the younger brother of the late Choi Moon-sung and the uncle of Choi Ki-tae—a man Jakyeong might have crossed paths with in Macau as a starving child.

Even fifteen years later, the bloody, suffocating knots of the past refused to untangle.

"Thank you for the meal, ma'am."

Leaving half his bowl untouched, Jakyeong rose from the table. The housekeeper asked with maternal concern if he was feeling unwell, but he offered a brief, reassuring smile and headed upstairs.

He methodically stripped, cleaned, and reassembled the suppressed firearms and combat blades for the upcoming strike, then stepped outside for a walk to clear the mental fog.

The night air remained thick with tropical humidity. Though the rain had paused, bruised storm clouds hung low, threatening another downpour. The perimeter guards bowed respectfully as he passed. The German Shepherd from before bounded through the trees, now accompanied by a pack of equally massive, well-trained patrol hounds.

After walking the grounds, Jakyeong returned inside, showered, and sat cross-legged on the floor for an hour of quiet meditation, methodically purging every stray thought from his mind.

When he finally opened his eyes, midnight had settled over the estate.

Standing by the panoramic glass, his eyes locked onto the pool below.

Kang Il-hyun was sitting alone in the dark on a teak chair by the coping, staring into the illuminated water. Fat raindrops were beginning to fall from the sky, but the man didn't move an inch.

He chain-smoked through several cigarettes in absolute stillness before slowly unbuttoning his black shirt, kicking off his shoes, and discarding his jacket onto the deck.

Jakyeong’s eyes widened as Il-hyun stepped into the water fully dressed in his slacks.

He drifted onto his back, floating face-up toward the dark sky.

Suspended in the turquoise water, his posture looked as serene and weightless as a man sleeping in his own bed.

The rain thickened, pelting the surface in violent ripples, yet Il-hyun remained floating like a corpse.

Jakyeong turned away from the glass, throwing himself onto the mattress. Let him soak. It's none of my business.

He closed his eyes, willing himself to sleep, but rest refused to come.

He sat up and marched back to the window. The man was still floating out there in the downpour.

Did he get plastered? If he drowns out there, who wires the rest of our money?

Or... is he drowning in something he can't endure? Why the hell pick tonight to act out a tragic melodrama?

Was his subdued demeanor over the past few days because of his mother's memorial? Can a monster like that actually feel grief?

Cursing under his breath, Jakyeong pulled on loose clothes and headed downstairs. The villa was dark and silent, the staff having turned in hours ago. The night-shift sentries at the terrace doors nodded as he stepped out into the storm.

Popping a large umbrella open, Jakyeong crossed the stone patio toward the pool.

The torrential rain drummed violently against the canvas. He came to a halt by the coping, looking down.

Il-hyun lay suspended in the water, his eyes shut tight, motionless.

"What are you doing?"

No answer.

"I asked what the hell you're doing."

Still dead silence.

Panic flared in Jakyeong's chest. Dropping the umbrella, he dove straight into the deep end, his hand clamping tight around Il-hyun's soaked arm.

Il-hyun’s eyes snapped open.

He stood upright in the waist-deep water, wiping the streaming droplets from his brow, arching a single dark brow in mild surprise.

Jakyeong let out a long, ragged exhale of pure relief, immediately following it with a furious, muttered curse.

Il-hyun tilted his head, studying him closely. "Why do you have that look on your face?"

"What look?" Jakyeong snapped defensively.

A faint, tender smile touched Il-hyun’s dripping lips.

"Why are you looking at me with such terrified eyes?"

Jakyeong’s dark pupils trembled.

The breath caught in his throat. Terrified? Me?

No. I was only worried our paycheck would sink to the bottom of the pool... He wanted to spit the excuse aloud, but the words withered on his tongue.

The sky opened up, unleashing a blinding wall of rain.

Il-hyun raised a massive palm, holding it tenderly over the crown of Jakyeong’s head to shield his face from the downpour. With his other hand, he gently brushed the streaming water from Jakyeong’s cheek with the pad of his thumb.

"Let's get out of the rain. You'll catch a cold."
